key_insight: DecompRL teaches an LLM to decompose hard coding tasks into modular sub-functions, making otherwise unreachable solutions tractable by recombining smaller implementations.
engineering_relevance: The approach shifts compute from expensive GPU sampling to cheaper CPU-based recombination and verification, reducing token cost while improving success on difficult code-generation benchmarks.
method: Use reinforcement learning to explicitly learn hierarchical code decomposition.
Generate multiple implementations per module and recombine them into candidate full solutions.
Evaluate many recombinations cheaply on CPU, turning one hard search into a modular search space.
evidence_signal: On LiveCodeBench and CodeContests with Qwen 2.5 7B and Code World Model 32B, DecompRL outperforms standard and diversity-optimized RL beyond 10^5 tokens per problem and cuts GPU token cost by about 50x.
watch_item: Performance depends on the ability to decompose tasks into independently solvable modules, so gains may be limited when a problem lacks a clean modular structure or when recombination introduces interface errors.
paper_title: DecompRL: Solving Harder Problems by Learning Modular Code Generation
